route: 8 (semantic coherence of the response distribution) + conditional-dependency asymmetry between the two linked items
evidence: Subscale membership is fixed by the source, not by statistics: S4 File states 'Numeracy 3 (item 42-44)' and these are the instrument's only 0/1-scored items. What is inferred is the within-subscale order num1/num2/num3 = items 42/43/44, and three content-implied predictions confirm it on n=582. (a) Items 43 (compute BMI) and 44 (classify that BMI) are cognitively dependent, item 42 (carbohydrate multiplication) is unrelated: r(num2,num3)=0.719 vs r(num1,num2)=0.174 and r(num1,num3)=0.110 -- this pins num1=42. (b) The dependency is asymmetric in the direction the assignment predicts: n(num2=1 & num3=0)=10 against n(num2=0 & num3=1)=60, i.e. P(num3=1|num2=1)=0.975 while P(num2=1|num3=1)=0.865 -- computing the BMI nearly forces the classification, but the classification is gettable without it (four printed alternatives). The reversed assignment num2=44/num3=43 predicts 60 vs 10 and is excluded. (c) Difficulty ordering matches content: p(num1)=0.875 (one multiplication, easiest) > p(num3)=0.766 (four-option choice with a guessing floor) > p(num2)=0.680 (open-ended calculation, hardest). NOT established: the paper publishes no per-item statistics, so none of this is a match against published numbers -- it is a test of content-implied predictions; and the routes do not independently confirm that num1-num3 are HELMA items 42-44 rather than some other three items, which rests on the S4 scoring manual and on these being the only binary-scored block in the instrument.
